subject: Identity wiring & provisioning proposal for Private Control Plane
messages:
From: Beth Jones <beth.jones@evergreen.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>; laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@evergreen.health; it-support@evergreen.health
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment identity questions

Hi Michael and team,

Thanks for the call this week. To move our private control plane onboarding forward we need a concise plan for how Redwood will wire SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and the RBAC mapping into our on-prem IdP. The security team also asked for a cert rotation cadence and proof of how service accounts will be scoped.

I've attached our requirements doc with a few redlines. High-level asks:
- SAML federation: support IdP-initiated SSO and SP-initiated SSO, metadata exchange through a secure link.
- SCIM: user and group sync, delta-based provisioning, support for custom attribute mappings (department, cost_center).
- RBAC: provide recommended role bindings and least-privilege templates for cross-account admins.
- Audit: describe audit log entries and retention for private control plane actions.

Can you send a short wiring diagram + one-page rollout plan? Our procurement team also wants an inventory of required public keys/certs and any firewall ports.

Attachments: evergreen_sso_requirements.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Beth
Director of IT Security
Evergreen Health

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Jones <beth.jones@evergreen.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@evergreen.health, it-support@evergreen.health
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Identity wiring & provisioning proposal for Private Control Plane

Beth, thanks for the clear asks — we can deliver a wiring diagram and a concise rollout plan by EOD tomorrow. Quick summary of what we'll provide:
- SAML: metadata XML for Redwood SP, support both IdP/SP initiated flows; we recommend signed assertions and HTTP-POST binding.
- SCIM: we'll provide a connector that supports SCIM 2.0 with change events (delta) + a mapping file (YAML) for department/cost_center; we'll include an opt-in bulk sync for initial import.
- RBAC: default role templates (viewer, operator, admin, billing) and a recommended delegated-admin pattern for your security admins.
- Audit & logs: control plane will emit audit records for authn/authz events to your log collector (syslog/rsyslog over TLS or an S3-compatible endpoint) with retention guidance.
- Cert rotation: propose 90-day rotation for SP certs; 30-day warning window with automated signing request (CSR) workflow.

Firewall/ports: mainly HTTPS (443) outbound from private control plane to Redwood managed endpoint for control plane heartbeats when using the hybrid model; if fully air-gapped we'll publish a list of ports for the install package.

I'll attach the diagram and the SCIM mapping draft. Laura — can you review the RBAC recommendations? Mina — look at the cert rotation flow and the CSR automation note. Vanessa I'll need a short procurement inventory for what we ship (public keys, CA chain, agent package).

Attachments: redwood-scim-mapping-draft.yaml (yaml); cert-rotation-proposal.md (md)

—Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Beth Jones <beth.jones@evergreen.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Identity wiring & provisioning proposal for Private Control Plane

Michael — quick confirmations from product/security POV:

1) Roles and least privilege
- Agree with viewer/operator/admin/billing templates. Add a "provisioner" role limited to SCIM write operations and entitlement changes (useful for HR/service accounts).
- Recommend we publish a mapping matrix that shows IdP groups -> Redwood roles and an example SCIM group claim mapping.

2) SAML assertions and attributes
- Require NameID format to be urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress or persistent ID depending on Evergreen preference.
- Include these attributes: email, given_name, family_name, department, cost_center, employee_id. Keep attribute names configurable.

3) Audit and retention
- We should offer a sample retention policy (90 days default, configurable to 1 year for enterprise). Provide an example syslog schema and sample event IDs.

4) Compliance artifacts
- We'll attach a short checklist showing SOC2-relevant artifacts we can provide for private deployments (audit logs, access lists, change history).

I'll add the "provisioner" role to the RBAC doc and update the mapping example. Mina — can you confirm the CSR automation supports 3rd-party KMS signing? That's a gate for their HSM requirement.

Laura
Product Manager, Private Deployment
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>; Beth Jones <beth.jones@evergreen.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Identity wiring & provisioning proposal for Private Control Plane

Quick technical check and open items: 

- CSR automation: our agent supports generating a CSR locally and pushing it to a customer-managed KMS/HSM for signing; we have an adapter for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and a PKCS#11 flow for on-prem HSMs. Note: offline/air-gapped KMS requires manual signing and import — we'll document the steps.

- SCIM rate limits: connector will respect IdP throttling; default incremental sync every 5m, but initial bulk import should be run once via a dry-run then execute full push. We should provide an idempotent partial-sync flag to avoid duplicate group memberships.

- SAML metadata exchange: recommend secure download link + short-lived metadata URL (signed) for initial setup; also provide a static metadata XML for customers that cannot fetch URLs.

- Ports and network: for hybrid (control plane calls home) we need outbound 443 to redwood-control.redwood.ai plus NTP. For fully private installs there is an embedded control plane and the admin console is reachable only within VPC — in that case we will provide a manifest for the ops team.

Open action items:
1) Vanessa — compile the procurement inventory (public cert, CA chain, agent package sizes, checksum).
2) Michael — send wiring diagram + RBAC mapping doc to Beth for approval.
3) Laura — add the provisioner role to RBAC matrix and publish a sample mapping.
4) Beth / Evergreen — confirm whether they prefer SP-initiated or IdP-initiated primary flow and whether the KMS will be customer-managed HSM.

I'll add the technical notes to the Confluence page and include examples for PKCS#11.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
